title: Shift-safe tenant quota reset with cross-pool lease transfer and delayed accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved-capacity tenants and standard tenants exhibit occasional double-counts or lost token consumption during quota reset boundaries when a tenant is live-migrated between pools or when delayed usage events arrive after a reset checkpoint. These failures show up as billing disputes and wrong throttles. This ticket defines a shift-safe reset mechanism that: 1) allows cross-pool lease transfer without losing in-flight usage, 2) preserves idempotent reset checkpoints for distributed reconciliations, and 3) supports delayed meter events that arrive up to a configured lag without inadvertently re-crediting or double-debiting tenants.

Scope: Engineering implementation across quota ledger, reset coordinator, tenant-lease manager, and billing reconciliation. Does NOT include UI changes in Console (follow-up ticket will add per-tenant reset logs view).
acceptance_criteria: Reset operations are idempotent: repeated commit attempts for the same epoch produce identical tenant balances and audit entries.

A tenant migrated between reserved pools during a reset window will have its in-flight KV cache and pending usage reconciled so the new pool continues consuming the same lease without double-counting.
Delayed usage events (arriving within configurable grace period, default 2 hours) are reconciled into the previous epoch ledger and do not cause negative balances or duplicate billing line items.
Telemetry shows no unexplained +/- adjustments for tenants exercising migration flow during the release rollout window (validated against synthetic load harness).
End-to-end integration tests covering cross-pool handoff, partial writes, leader failover, and late-arriving events pass in CI.
implementation_plan: Introduce a lightweight Reset Epoch record with fields: epoch_id (string), snapshot_checkpoint_ts (ISO8601), tenant_watermarks (serialized list as single string), commit_proof (string). Store in global ledger with monotonic version.

Change lease-transfer protocol: before moving a tenant lease, current pool creates a Transfer Intent record and streams buffered pending-usage to transfer object; destination pool acknowledges and replays any pending usage bounded by snapshot_checkpoint_ts.

Modify quota debit path to annotate usage events with event_arrival_ts and epoch_id; if event_arrival_ts <= snapshot_checkpoint_ts + grace_window, mark for previous-epoch reconciliation, else apply to current epoch.
Add a replayable reconciliation job that consumes late-marked events and appends them to the previous epoch ledger with dedicated audit entries so billing remains auditable.
Add deterministic conflict resolution: last-writer is checkpointed via commit_proof; concurrent resets compare commit_proof and higher lexicographic proof wins and other commits become no-ops.
Backfill and test: run synthetic migration load against staging, run billing reconciliation and compare to golden ledger to validate no variance beyond 0.01% for synthetic tenants.
telemetry_and_rollout: Emit metric quota.reset.attempts and quota.reset.commits with labels: epoch_id, region, pool_id, tenant_type.
Emit gauge tenant.reset.inflight_transfers and a histogram for late_events_lag_seconds.
Release rollout: feature-flagged on per-team canary tenants for 48 hours, then 10% traffic, then 100% if metrics stable.
Pre-rollout check: run replay on a 7-day window in staging with parity check against existing billing ledger.
Post-rollout monitoring: alert if (billing_adjustments_rate > 0.1% over baseline) or (quota_reset_error_rate > 0.01%).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Longer reconciliation window increases state to retain and increases CPU for replay jobs. Mitigation: default grace_window = 2 hours and configurable per-tenant; cap retention for late-marked events at 7 days.

Risk: Transfer Intent races during leader failover could leave transfer incomplete. Mitigation: transfer intent is idempotent and persisted to the ledger; destination must ack before source marks lease released.

Risk: Incorrect tagging of event epoch_id leads to mis-billing. Mitigation: add end-to-end integration tests and memoized per-request epoch resolution logic with unit tests, plus audit log entries for every event that changes epoch mapping.
Risk: Increased storage for extra audit entries. Mitigation: compact committed epochs after 90 days into compressed audit archive with cryptographic summary kept online.
